shared_elements: low relief carving on a flat stone slab
repeated small units forming a patterned band (curls/beads vs. rows of animals)
justification: Both are low-relief slabs with profile figures and a horizontal patterned band, but A depicts a single large naturalistic human head and torso with elaborately curled beard, hair, earring and headgear, while B depicts multiple small schematic animals (quadrupeds, birds, a snake-like form) stacked in registers with no human figure. The only correspondences are the very generic ones of profile depiction and banded organisation, which any relief tradition could produce independently.
